test_title: PYST 72: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A water tank can be filled in 13 minutes using 46 identical pipes. How long (in minutes) will it take to fill the same tank if only 27 such pipes are used? (Round off the answer to two decimal places.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time ∝ 1 / number of pipes

New time = Old time × (Old pipes ÷ New pipes)

= 13 × (46 ÷ 27)

= 598 ÷ 27 ≈ 22.15 minutes

**∴ Answer = 22.15 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

46 pipes fill tank in 13 minutes

Required: time taken by 27 pipes

**Formula used:**

Time × Number of pipes = Constant work

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total work = 46 × 13 = 598 pipe-minutes

⇒ Time with 27 pipes = 598 ÷ 27

⇒ Time ≈ 22.15 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 22.15 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion

Time and number of pipes are inversely proportional.

Work Formula

Work = Rate × Time. Here rate depends on number of pipes.

Pipe Concept

More pipes reduce time proportionally for same work.
